newsitem.title: USA: Oscar-winning figures returned to creator.
newsitem.headline: Oscar-winning figures returned to creator.

text.p: Wallace and Gromit, two plasticine figures that starred in last year's Oscar-winning short "A Close Shave", were returned to their creator on Monday after being left in the trunk of a taxi over the weekend.

A spokeswoman for British creator Nick Park said Wallace and his dog Gromit were returned early on Monday morning by the taxi driver who drove Park to his Manhattan hotel Saturday when he arrived in New York for a publicity tour.
"I saw Nick this morning, he was smiling ear to ear when he went out the door," said spokeswoman Cheryl Difatta.

The models of Wallace on his motorcycle and Gromit in a sidecar were last seen on Saturday in their travel case in the trunk of a cab. A porter at Park's hotel failed to notice the case in the cab's trunk, and the driver drove away with them. Police said the loss had been reported.
The puppets have starred in such hit short films as "The Wrong Trousers," "A Grand Day Out" and "A Close Shave," which won an Oscar in 1996 for Best Animated Short Film.
